newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-GLORY AND BIG DOLLARS ON OFFER FOR SYDNEY-HOBART RECORD.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-GLORY AND BIG DOLLARS ON OFFER FOR SYDNEY-HOBART RECORD.

text.p: The 1996 Sydney-to-Hobart yacht race will offer A$300,000 (US$237,000) to the first boat to break the 21-year-old race record, organisers said on Tuesday.
But they said money would not be the main incentive for any crews out to capture the line honours record in one of the world's great ocean races which starts on December 26.

"While there is a A$300,000 prize, the money is going to be less important than the emotional and psychological victory of taking away a record that's stood for 21 years," said Peter Bush, commodore of the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia.
The prize is A$50,000 higher than last year.

The race record of two days 14 hours 36 minutes 56 seconds was set in 1975 by U.S. maxi yacht Kialoa. The closest any yacht has come to the record was in 1994, when the ketch Tasmania finished just over two hours outside Kialoa's mark.
The organisers said a strong fleet of international yachts would contest the 630-nautical mile race this year. Bush said he hoped 1995 line honours winner, U.S. maxi Sayonara, would defend its title.
Sayonara's crew in last year's race included media magnate Rupert Murdoch, a friend of the yacht's American owner, computer company chief executive Larry Ellison.

The participation of Murdoch drew international attention to the race, particularly after he tore away half the top of his right index finger during a warm-up race on board the 23.7 metre (78 foot) Sayonara.
Asked if Murdoch would race again this year, Bush said: "We probably won't know until the last minute."
Among the entries confirmed is the maxi Exile, owned by expatriate Australian businessman Warwick Miller.
"Pound for pound and foot for foot, all the designers say Exile is the fastest maxi in the world," Bush said.
Maxis are boats longer than 60 feet (18.3 metres) and are favoured for race line honours because of their huge sail area.
